title: fix(update): honor TMPDIR without filling home
body:
Fixes #177707

## What Problem This Solves

An update can fill the home/state volume even when `TMPDIR` points to a roomy volume, then fail while recording recovery state.

## User Impact

Update-time runtime copies, plugin source captures, and SQLite inspection snapshots honor `TMPDIR` (SQLite retains an explicit `XDG_CACHE_HOME` override). Optional original-state captures stay beside state for durable recovery discovery, but check their known payload budget before writing and warn when there is insufficient space. npm's independent cache and the locations that must remain with the installation/state are documented.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retained-runtime owner preferred a sibling even with explicit `TMPDIR`; plugin capture and SQLite snapshot owners defaulted to state/home storage; the original-capture owner only budgeted its databases, not declared file resources. Reuse those owners: respect explicit scratch placement and check the existing file inventory plus metadata headroom, including a second check after database acquisition. Required rollback and live-authority checks remain intact. Disk-full worker recovery already landed in #176902; this change does not replace it.

Production: +46/-8 (net +38); tests: +166/-116 (net +50); docs: +18. Necessary growth is the file-payload space check and four distinct placement/capacity regressions. An existing retention test moves to its owner suite to keep the database backup suite under its line budget. No new configuration, schema, dependencies, or parallel storage owner.

## Evidence

- Four regressions fail on the unmodified base and pass with the fix: runtime `TMPDIR` selection, byte-neutral SQLite inspection in `TMPDIR`, temporary plugin capture placement, and refusing an oversized original capture before creating its destination.
- Production types, infra/plugin test types, touched-file lint/format, dependency cycles, and documentation links pass. The lint fallback was checked with a temporary `debugger` canary, then run clean after restoring it.
- Final independent Codex review: no actionable P0/P1 findings.

- Live packaged Linux proof on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m5bv46p6n7fn848dpk2nzgx5`: isolated 2 GiB home filesystem, roomy `TMPDIR` and npm prefix/cache, and a synthetic plugin with a 128 MiB declared Doctor backup resource. `openclaw update --tag "$artifact" --yes --json --no-restart` failed with `ENOSPC` on the baseline; removing only the proof ballast allowed `openclaw update repair --yes --json --no-restart` and retry to exit 0. With the fix installed, the same 96 MiB free-space setup exited 0, warned that the capture needed **194 MiB versus 93 MiB available**, and left large capture bytes unchanged at 372,576,256. After freeing space, repair/retry/status/config validation all exited 0; sealed manifests and SHA-256 checks verified the complete 128 MiB payload. No operator state or Gateway was used. One fixture setup rerun was needed because packing the fixed artifact cleared the baseline tarball; the baseline was recovered from its isolated cache and its original SHA-256 verified before the successful comparison.

- Clean latest-stable upgrade: installed `openclaw@latest` (2026.10.5, published build `1b58cb9a1b4f`) in a separate isolated home/prefix, then ran `openclaw update --tag "$fixed" --yes --json --no-restart`. Result: `status: ok`, `mode: npm`, installed fixed build `a8bc87f1c5b1`, config validation `{ "valid": true, "warnings": [] }`. The Testbox was stopped after proof.

- All 40 touched/direct-importer test files ran locally with isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and private `TMPDIR`, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <selected files> --maxWorkers=1`: **37 files passed, 3 platform/service-guarded files skipped; 445 tests passed, 22 skipped; all eight shards passed in 1,525.90 s**. This includes the existing full-agent-database-write recovery regression. Source verification completed after the run.

Existing slow proof remains visible: the backup file spent 167.7 s across real isolated captures, and the CLI admission file spent 331.2 s across real initialization/capture/failure paths. Its existing invalid-dev-target case took 33.0 s; the existing-state/refused original-capture case took 32.1 s. The Doctor partial-migration/retry preservation case took 60.5 s and performs eight real captures plus semantic comparisons. These are unchanged integration paths, not new waits; the added capacity case took 1.8 s in the full run. No timeout, retry, assertion, or baseline was relaxed. The package build also emitted an unrelated locale-size warning from the unchanged Control UI.

The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the campaign's local gate budget. The repository lint wrapper's declaration preparation hit the host's 300 s timeout, so the approved direct lint check was used. Existing test-shard inventory budgets are inherited (`gateway-root` 726/720; `plugins-platform` 727/720); no budget or baseline was changed. PR CI remains the broad proof.
